clue.text: French author ends with monstrous woman making cheese

indicators.note: the French author ends the answer, so his name comes after the monstrous woman

parts.note: a Gorgon is one of the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth, such as Medusa
Emile Zola was the French novelist of Germinal

explanation.surface: A French writer's story ends with a monster woman producing a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese named after a town near Milan.

clue.text: Throw back first old Greek coin

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word old, and also puts it at the front
back means the word for throw is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to lob is to throw something in a high arc

explanation.surface: Someone tosses an ancient Greek coin back over their shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Old priest finds bible in hotel room

explanation.surface: A visitor to a hotel turns up a religious book left there by an old cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Gideon is a hero of the Book of Judges who built an altar and offered sacrifice, which the setter stretches to priest; the Gideons are the society that leaves bibles in hotel rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament leader offered sacrifices like a priest, and a copy of scripture placed in a hotel bedroom by the Gideons society is called by his name.

clue.text: Baby born, over a time, Edward I

parts.note: ne, French for born, is used before a man's original name
on can mean over, as in a book on (about) a subject

indicators.note: the Roman numeral one, as in a king's title, asks for the first letter of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A list of royal births noting that Edward I was born after a certain time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edward I' reads as the king, but the I asks for Edward's letter number one, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, in its first weeks of life.

clue.text: Large cow straddling the line, or antelope

indicators.note: straddling means the word for a large cow sits either side of the word for the line

parts.note: an ox is a large bovine animal, a cow or bull
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A big cow standing astride a boundary line, or perhaps it is an antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large straight-horned antelope of African and Arabian deserts.

clue.text: Old boy, a smoker, meeting students

parts.note: a lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney, something that smokes
NUS is the National Union of Students in Britain

explanation.surface: A former pupil who smokes falls in with a group of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' suggests a person with cigarettes; here it is the chimney, LUM, a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old boy is a former pupil of a school, which is what an alumnus is.

clue.text: Leave for low hills in search of birds

parts.note: to part is to leave or go away
ridges are long narrow stretches of raised ground

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for the hills to hunt game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Partridges are plump game birds of the pheasant family, shot in autumn.

clue.text: They might bring 7 back

parts.note: read as dogs that fetch the shot game birds of seven down back to the hunter

explanation.definitionFit: Retrievers are gun dogs trained to fetch shot game for the hunter.

clue.text: Post spoken of for this chap

indicators.note: spoken of signals that the word for post is heard rather than written

parts.note: the post is the mail delivered to a house

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the letters to be read out to a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: A male is a man or boy, any fellow.

clue.text: Go, your food is cooked (well done)

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of your food have been doctored and rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: A cook tells a diner to go ahead: their meal is ready, cooked well done.
explanation.walkthrough: '(well done)' looks like a note on the steak, but it is the definition, praise for an achievement; GO stands as written before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Good for you is an exclamation of congratulation, praise for an achievement.

clue.text: Get the better of employer

explanation.definitionFit: To master a rival is to overcome them, and a master is also the boss who hires servants or apprentices.

clue.text: Sebastian can fly in with relative

indicators.note: in means the word for fly is placed inside the athlete's surname

parts.note: Sebastian Coe is the British Olympic middle-distance runner
a gnat is a small two-winged fly

explanation.surface: An athlete is able to fly in with a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related by birth, and as a noun a cognate is a blood relation.

clue.text: Common love and desire invoke pity

parts.note: passion is strong love and sexual desire

explanation.surface: Shared love and longing call forth sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is sympathetic concern for the suffering of others.

clue.text: £1,000 given to relation, or her daughter perhaps

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
a niece is a relation, a sibling's daughter

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds is left to a relative, or possibly to her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' refers back to the relation, the niece: her daughter is one example of the answer, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece's daughter is a grandniece, also called a great-niece.

clue.text: Legally preclude two points for best conclusion

parts.note: E and S are compass points, east and south
top means best, the highest finish, and the setter adds conclusion to say it goes at the end

explanation.surface: Two marks awarded for the best ending in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' suggests a score; they are compass points. 'for best conclusion' just says the word for best comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a law term meaning to bar someone from asserting something contrary to what they said before.

clue.text: The gold mace, for example, may be an omen

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
mace is a spice made from the covering of the nutmeg seed

explanation.surface: A golden ceremonial mace might be taken as a portent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mace' suggests the ceremonial staff, especially next to gold; here it is the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is a sign or portent, originally from watching the flight of birds.

clue.text: A Norse god, for example, seen flying

indicators.note: seen means the abbreviation for example shows up within the word for flying

parts.note: something flying is in the air
eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A Norse deity, say, is spotted flying through the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegir is the giant who personifies the sea in Norse mythology.

clue.text: Letters written in distress, especially

indicators.note: written in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone notes that letters are often written in times of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Esses are the letters S, the spelt-out name of the letter.

clue.text: The fellow has nothing to complain of

indicators.note: has means the word for fellow holds the zero inside it

parts.note: a man is a fellow
O looks like the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A contented man has no grounds for complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To moan is to grumble or grouse.

clue.text: Love the expression of surprise on seeing moulding!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
gee is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A lover exclaims in surprise at the sight of some fancy plasterwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogee is an S-shaped moulding with a concave and a convex curve.

clue.text: The officer in charge is an awful pain

parts.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: The commanding officer is a real pain to work for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer in charge' looks like one phrase, the boss, but it splits into an officer's rank and the short form of in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe spasmodic pain in the abdomen, common in babies.

clue.text: Remedy ingested last month for laboratory bacteria

indicators.note: ingested means the word for remedy swallows the abbreviation for last month

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
ult, short for ultimo, means of last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A medicine swallowed last month treated a bacterial infection.
explanation.walkthrough: ULT (ultimo) is old commercial shorthand for 'of last month'.
explanation.definitionFit: A culture is a population of bacteria grown in a lab on a nutrient medium.

clue.text: He takes money for fare

parts.note: reads like a bus conductor collecting fares, but the fare is food served for payment

explanation.definitionFit: A caterer is paid to supply food and drink at functions, and fare means food.

clue.text: A divine dessert rejected, containing one-third egg, which made sense

indicators.note: containing means the run built from a, divine and dessert holds a letter of egg inside it

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, so a divine

indicators.note: rejected means the word for dessert is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a dessert

indicators.note: one-third of the three-letter word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns down a pudding with a little egg in it, which seemed logical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the dessert backwards; the letter from egg goes inside the run built from a, divine and that reversed dessert, straight after the divine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that added up was consistent and made sense, as with a column of figures that tallies.

clue.text: The pharaoh who could see Mars

indicators.note: could here hints that the letters of the following words could be arranged into the name

explanation.surface: An ancient king who could gaze at the red planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses (Ramses) was the name of several Egyptian kings, most famously Rameses II.

clue.text: Hesitation — double hesitation — in naming a rare metal

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
bi- is a prefix meaning two or double
um is another sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone stammers repeatedly when trying to name an uncommon metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Erbium is a soft silvery element of the rare-earth group.

clue.text: The ghost might sit and rest in peace shortly

indicators.note: might hints that the letters could form a new word when shuffled

parts.note: RIP is the abbreviation for rest in peace, seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A ghost might sit down and rest in peace for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' is the anagram signal: the word sit and the gravestone abbreviation are shuffled together as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit is a disembodied soul, a phantom or spectre.

clue.text: A military force returning from a long way away

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for the military force is read back to front

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: An air force squadron flying home from a distant posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great distance.

clue.text: A dry diocese in the right place

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for right is put within the word for diocese

parts.note: a see is the diocese of a bishop

explanation.surface: A diocese with no drink is in exactly the right place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere means withered and dry, as of leaves.

clue.text: Peacekeepers excused, but not pardoned

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
forgiven means excused or let off

explanation.surface: UN troops are let off but still not pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Unforgiven means not granted forgiveness.

clue.text: Concerning the church at one time

parts.note: on means about or concerning; that the run of letters also sits inside this word is a coincidence
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A note about a church in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, in the past.

clue.text: Somehow take temperature — lacking energy — need help to hear

indicators.note: somehow means the letters end up in some new arrangement
lacking means one letter is dropped from the word temperature

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A patient running a fever and short of energy needs some help to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops one E (energy) from TEMPERATURE, and 'Somehow' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear trumpet is an old horn-shaped hearing aid held to the ear.
